summary: Audit schema evolution: deprecated fields breaking customer SIEM enrichment and request for compatibility bridge and compliance evidence
description: Issue summary: Mariner Payments reports that a recent audit schema change (audit-schema-v2) deprecated several commonly used fields (actor.email, session.id, request.client_ip) and introduced replacement fields (actor.principal_email, session.token, request.network.ip_v4). Impact: Their SIEM enrichment pipeline (internal to Mariner) relies on exact field names and now fails to map user identity and session linkage for ~7% of events, causing missed alerts for MFA bypass patterns and audit gaps for compliance checks. They are requesting: 1) temporary compatibility bridge or mapping layer for exports so their SIEM mapping works without immediate customer-side changes, 2) canonical field mapping documentation and migration timeline, and 3) signed evidence package for auditors showing: hashes/timestamps for exported batches, sample retention proof for 90-day window, and confirmation that no deletion occurred for the affected window. Environment: production (us-east) exports to customer-managed Splunk HEC and S3 archive. Timeline: issue first observed 2026-03-09 at ~14:30 UTC when daily ingest alert counts dropped. Customer provided sample export with both old and new field names for the same time window. Attachments: sample_csv_export_20260309.csv (customer), mapping_snippets.txt (customer).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Redwood audit export to send daily batch to S3 + Splunk HEC
2) Use existing SIEM field mapping that expects actor.email and session.id
3) Observe enrichment failures and missing identity joins for events after 2026-03-09 00:00 UTC
4) Compare exported payloads and note replaced field names in audit-schema-v2 batches
logs: 2026-03-09T14:31:02Z export-service INFO exported batch id=8f3a2c size=8124 records schema=audit-schema-v2
2026-03-09T14:31:10Z siem-connector WARN failed-mapping count=612 field=actor.email missing
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: upstream schema roll-out toggled to v2 for a subset of tenants in us-east during a staged rollout
Confirmed via ingestion logs that the batch was labeled audit-schema-v2 and contains replacement fields actor.principal_email and session.token
Checked rollout gating: no config flags found for Mariner Payments specifically (possible global phased flag triggered)
Reproducer: running local transform script that renames actor.principal_email -> actor.email restores SIEM enrichment for provided sample
Risk assessment: ~7% event loss for identity joins reported by customer; no evidence of dropped records, only field name changes affecting downstream parsing
Data proof request: customer asked for signed batch manifest for the affected window and retention confirmation for 2026-01-01..2026-04-01 timeframe

resolution: Temporary tenant-scoped compatibility bridge (export transform that maps actor.principal_email -> actor.email, session.token -> session.id, request.network.ip_v4 -> request.client_ip) deployed to prod-us-east for Mariner Payments. SRE created signed manifest generation for affected batches (signed with export service key) and produced an evidence bundle including: sample batch JSON, SHA256 digest, RFC3161 timestamp for signature, and retention statement. Action items: 1) Share migration guide and canonical field matrix with customer; 2) Create follow-up ticket for full schema rollout automated compatibility test (INT-412); 3) Remove compatibility bridge after customer confirms migration (max 30 days). Customer accepted workaround on 2026-03-12 and requested auditor bundle; bundle delivered via secure SFTP and confirmation sent.
